title: Polarimetric collagen features classify breast-tumor regions in a limited tissue study
summary: First posted in May 2021 and journal-published in 2022, this study used logistic regression on polarimetric second-harmonic-generation and texture features to distinguish tumor from normal breast-tissue regions. From one microarray originally containing 45 cores from 12 patients, the analysis retained 15 normal and 20 tumor cores; prediction on two held-out cores from that same array reported 91.3% subimage accuracy. Random subimage cross-validation and the small core-level hold-out do not establish patient-independent diagnosis, external validation or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Logistic-regression classifier on polarimetric second-harmonic-generation and collagen-texture features
organization: University of Toronto; University of Toronto Mississauga; Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University Health Network; National Centre of Pathology; Vilnius University; Light Conversion

evidence.tested: A binary logistic-regression classifier used 33 image-derived features and 544 normal/543 tumor subimages, evaluated using 1,000 repeated stratified five-fold partitions. Two cores (one normal, one tumor) were set aside before training; subimage prediction in these cores reported accuracy 91.3% and F1 90.7%. The original publisher PDF Fig. 5 and Results report cross-validation accuracy 94.2%; those performance measures are not interpreted as patient-level accuracy.
evidence.unknown: The Methods treat subimages as data points without establishing patient/core-grouped cross-validation. Held-out prediction uses only two cores from the same microarray; external or patient-independent validation was not established. Adipose/no-signal areas and two rare stromal tumor cores were excluded, and subimage size affects predictive performance. Clinical utility, prospective workflow performance and patient benefit were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression learns a normal-versus-tumor classifier from collagen ultrastructure statistics and texture features measured by widefield P-SHG microscopy, linking the learned operation to a specific ex-vivo tissue classification result.

source_review.scope: Original bioRxiv v1 abstract/date/affiliations and original journal publisher PDF: abstract, classification Results, Fig. 5/table, Statistical analysis and machine learning Methods, tissue-microarray Methods and Discussion. PDF Fig. 5 also visually checked. Supplementary files not assessed.
